text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident P1003 fired: canary probe 'synth-canary-eu-west' flapping in eu-west-1 (3/5 probes failing). Details: https://pdt.redwood/p/INC-P1003

pagerduty: Auto-escalation: initial pager sent to primary on-call (alex kim).

alex kim: ack'd. I'll take it. starting triage.

marta g: seeing 503/502 cluster on the canary traffic window. spike started ~1948112000. Rolling failure rate ~45% -> now ~68% for the last 5m.

jin park: confirmed in grafana: canary latency up, error rate jump is correlated with requests that hit the new routing rule (route-id: r-aurora).

samir patel: weird — only the synthetic probes are failing, prod user traffic nominal. could be probe payload or header mismatch with the upstream change from this morning.

alex kim: good catch. can we replay a probe locally? marta, can you paste the last example probe payload/response?

marta g: paste: ```http
POST /synth-check HTTP/1.1
Host: synth-eu-west.redwood.internal
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "probe_id":"synth-canary-eu-west",
  "path":"/v1/ping",
  "expected_status":200
}

Response 502 from r-aurora (upstream reset)
```

jin park: running `curl -v` against /v1/ping on a canary host — seeing `upstream reset by peer` and a TLS negotiation churn immediately before the reset.

incident-bot: Note: probe fanout throttling active (20% reduction) due to automated backoff policy.

alex kim: mitigation proposal: 1) pause synth fanout for eu-west probes to stop noisy alerts, 2) add temporary routing fallback to r-aurora-backup, 3) keep monitoring for user-facing errors. Who can flip the probe pause?

oncall-rotation: ping @marta g to pause — she has synth permissions. also tagging SRE team for routing change.

marta g: pausing synth canary for eu-west now. Command: `/synth pause --id=synth-canary-eu-west --reason="investigating flapping"`  — done. probe status -> paused :white_check_mark:

samir patel: routing fallback tested in staging. command to promote backup: `infra route promote r-aurora-backup --region eu-west --dry-run` then remove dry-run when ready. can someone run the promote?

jin park: executing promote now (will apply safe drain). logs: ```INFO promoting r-aurora-backup -> drain=60s
INFO route promoted, 95% of canaries now served by backup
```

alex kim: monitoring metrics. error rate on synth hosts falling to baseline in 45s. user traffic still green.

marta g: creating a short incident note in the tracker: https://incidents.redwood/INC-P1003 with timeline and actions.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: P1003 acknowledged by alex kim. Escalation paused.

alex kim: brief impact summary for handoff: canary probes in eu-west flapped due to TLS upstream resets after routing rule change this morning. No customer-facing errors observed. We paused the synth fanout and promoted backup route r-aurora-backup. Root cause still under investigation (possible routing config + upstream TLS timing).

jin park: collecting tcpdump + TLS client-hello traces and will attach to the ticket.

marta g: tagging owners for a follow-up postmortem: @infra-team, @edge-team.

alex kim: handing off to night on-call @oncall-rotation for monitoring. next steps: continue root cause debug, validate rollback vs routing fix, and restore synth canary once patch verified. Leaving the incident open for postmortem.

oncall-rotation: acked handoff. I'll watch alerts overnight and escalate if anything changes. leaving a note in the ticket with current runbook steps. :spiral_calendar:

samir patel: small follow-up — will add a temporary test that simulates synth payloads against both r-aurora and r-aurora-backup.

alex kim: thanks everyone. closing slack thread for now, will update the incident doc with findings later. :thumbsup:
